x_notes.deprecated: as of 0.4.0 (v3.1) this table has NO producers and NO consumers: the entry gate weighs no price, brake inputs are computed per-dispatch or read from the boot-probe record (contract/probe.schema.json), and the collector no longer appends constants rows. Existing files remain valid history and still validate against this schema — the oneOf branches below are retained solely as the legal basis for historical rows. The notes that follow (row_identity, reading_state_machine, producers) describe the retired mechanism, kept for reading those rows
x_notes.table: one per-operator append-only JSONL file keyed task_family × harness × model_gen; the file path is named by each harness binding at the operator level; ships empty (no seeded values)
x_notes.row_identity: constants rows are cited as <key>@<provenance.run_id>/<provenance.ts>; discipline-price rows as <key>@<pair_run_ids joined with +>/<provenance.ts> — consumers cite row identity, never bare keys (append-only tables hold many rows per key)
x_notes.reading_state_machine: per key: first measured row is consumable (bootstrap); later changes land proposed (not consumable) until a human promotes (supersede-by-append). discipline-price rows have no proposed state: each ablation pair appends measured directly; a re-measurement supersedes only on human promote. unverifiable rows are never consumable — they exist for degradation counting and audit only
x_notes.family_unknown: key.family 'unknown' is legal ONLY on unverifiable rows (the journal carried no family declaration — degradation must not mis-bucket into a real family's counts); consumable row kinds (constants, discipline-price) always carry a real family
x_notes.producers: constants rows: the binding's tier-0 collector at precedent-append time (journal + binding-declared offered surfaces only). discipline-price rows: an ablation pair ONLY (same task, 0-worker form vs bare) — a single run's collector never produces one
x_notes.append_discipline: file-lock serialized, single-line atomic append (cross-project concurrency safe); 'first row' = file order
